primary_topics: Guest of honor and speaker address at the TOFIL (The Outstanding Filipino) Awards, December 12, 2006 -- CJP's first major appearance after his December 6, 2006 retirement; invited by Insular Life CEO Vicente Ayllon
CJP's first post-retirement self-presentation: 'a life of retirement, but not of resignation'; personal vignettes of his new life (tennis, golf, boogie, tango, dinner with Leni)

Four TOFIL awardees: Fr. Rocky Evangelista (Tuloy Foundation, street children); Antonio Meloto (Gawad Kalinga, Magsaysay awardee 2006); Ramon Orlina (glass artist); Socorro Ramos (National Book Store founder)
Three Es of a life worth living: excellence (give your best); ethics (internalize integrity, courage, prudence); eternity (our final destiny, account for everything)
sub_topics: Retirement context: CJP told Insular Life CEO Vicente Ayllon in September that he would no longer be CJ at the event time; Ayllon assured him his retirement didn't affect the invitation; 'As mandated by our Constitution, I was automatically retired as Chief Justice of the Philippines when I turned 70 at midnight of December 6, 2006'

Post-retirement self-presentation: 'I may be looking forward to a life of retirement, but I am certainly not ready to settle into a life of complacency. While my knees may start to hurt once in a while when I play tennis or golf, I assure you that I can still do a mean boogie or tango. Retirement gives me the time and opportunity to invite my wife Leni to have a quiet dinner at our favorite restaurant, hold her hands and whisper sweet nothings as I did 50 years ago, when I was still a carefree swain trying to impress her.'
TOFIL founding principle: established in 1988 on the belief that 'age was not an obstacle to achievement and passion not the sole province of the young'

Four awardees: (1) Fr. Marciano Rocky G. Evangelista, SDB -- Tuloy Foundation; education and rehabilitation of street children and at-risk out-of-school youth; (2) Antonio Meloto -- Gawad Kalinga; homes for slum dwellers; 2006 Ramon Magsaysay Foundation awardee; (3) Ramon G. Orlina -- glass sculptor; masterpieces cut, ground and polished from glass; proclaims Filipino genius internationally; (4) Socorro C. Ramos -- grand dame of book publishing; National Book Store; 'feeding and shaping the minds of generations'

Three Es: (1) Excellence -- 'demands that we give our best in whatever it is we decide to do. It requires not just competence, but also dedication to duty and hard work. It is the continuous pursuit of excellence that empowers us to constantly move forward and beyond'; (2) Ethics -- 'calls for internalizing the old-fashioned principles of integrity, courage and prudence. It is the use of our talents and gifts towards a society that is morally upright. At the end of life's long journey, it is the knowledge of having championed what is right'; (3) Eternity -- 'our life's final destiny. At the end of life's journey, we will account for everything we have done. Thus, in everything we think, say or do, we must set our sights beyond the here and now to our life hereafter'

Salonga's teaching: 'God is not finished with us. For life is a long, continuing process. In a deeper sense, we are all in process, always in a state of becoming, always in a period of transition, since all of us are en route on some kind of never-ending journey.'

one_paragraph_summary: Delivered December 12, 2006 -- six days after his mandatory retirement -- as guest of honor and speaker at the TOFIL (The Outstanding Filipino) Awards hosted by Insular Life (CEO Vicente Ayllon), this is CJP's first major post-retirement public address. He explains his presence: he told Ayllon in September that he would no longer be CJ; Ayllon assured him that his retirement did not affect the invitation. His first post-retirement self-portrait: 'I may be looking forward to a life of retirement, but I am certainly not ready to settle into a life of complacency. While my knees may start to hurt once in a while when I play tennis or golf, I assure you that I can still do a mean boogie or tango. Retirement gives me the time and opportunity to invite my wife Leni to have a quiet dinner at our favorite restaurant, hold her hands and whisper sweet nothings as I did 50 years ago, when I was still a carefree swain trying to impress her.' He presents the four TOFIL awardees: Fr. Rocky Evangelista (Tuloy Foundation, street children rehabilitation); Antonio Meloto (Gawad Kalinga, homes for slum dwellers, 2006 Magsaysay awardee); Ramon Orlina (glass sculptor, proclaims Filipino genius internationally); and Socorro Ramos (NBS founder, 'feeding and shaping the minds of generations'). Their embodiment of three Es: (1) Excellence -- 'demands that we give our best... the continuous pursuit of excellence empowers us to constantly move forward'; (2) Ethics -- 'internalizing the old-fashioned principles of integrity, courage and prudence... at the end of life's long journey, it is the knowledge of having championed what is right'; (3) Eternity -- 'our life's final destiny... we will account for everything we have done... we must set our sights beyond the here and now to our life hereafter.' He closes with Salonga's teaching: 'God is not finished with us. For life is a long, continuing process. In a deeper sense, we are all in process, always in a state of becoming, always in a period of transition, since all of us are en route on some kind of never-ending journey.'
